## Episode Thesis

This is a special episode of the Danish Investeringspodcasten with Hansen and Larsen. It is an interview with Denmark's tax and growth minister, Jacob Engelsmith, about capital taxation and almost nothing else. He backs tripling the aktiesparekonto (share savings account) to DKK 500k, raising the threshold for the lower share-gains tax rate, a 3-point cut to corporate tax, and removing the mellemskat (middle-bracket income tax). He also wants a Danish version of the French Tibi model to steer pension capital into scale-ups, and says the Copenhagen exchange has had more delistings than new listings. No stock-level recommendations are made: the minister declines to give investment advice. He points to Sweden as the benchmark, is upbeat about Danish growth, and warns of an economic slowdown, a rising-rate environment and an energy squeeze in Europe this winter.
